questions.question: What does "AI" stand for?
questions.note: The term has been used since the 1950s for machines that mimic human thinking.

questions.question: Who coined the term "artificial intelligence" in 1956?
questions.note: McCarthy proposed the 1956 Dartmouth workshop where the field got its name.

questions.question: In "ChatGPT", what does GPT stand for?
questions.note: It is "generative" because it creates text, and "pre-trained" on huge amounts of writing.

questions.question: Which company created ChatGPT?
questions.note: Microsoft is a big investor in OpenAI, but OpenAI built ChatGPT.

questions.question: The Turing Test checks whether...
questions.option_1: a computer can calculate faster than a human
questions.option_2: a machine's conversation is indistinguishable from a human's
questions.option_4: a robot can walk like a human
questions.note: Alan Turing proposed it in 1950, calling it the "imitation game".

questions.question: ChatGPT was released to the public in which year?
questions.note: November 30, 2022. It reached a million users in about five days.

questions.question: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated which world chess champion?
questions.note: The first computer to beat a reigning world champion in a full match.

questions.question: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016 at which game?
questions.note: Go has far more possible positions than chess, so this was a landmark.

questions.question: IBM's Watson won which TV quiz show in 2011?
questions.option_2: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
questions.note: It beat champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter.

questions.question: Who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on neural networks?
questions.note: Their work from the 1980s underpins modern machine learning.

questions.question: AlphaFold, whose creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, predicts what?
questions.note: Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of Google DeepMind, with David Baker.

questions.question: ELIZA, written in the 1960s at MIT, was an early example of what?
questions.note: ELIZA played a simple therapist; some users were convinced it understood them.

questions.question: In machine learning, a model mainly learns from...
questions.note: Instead of following hand-written rules, it finds patterns in examples.

questions.question: What is "training data"?
questions.option_1: The examples a model learns patterns from
questions.option_2: The electricity a data center uses
questions.note: Better and more varied training data usually means a better model.

questions.question: When an AI chatbot states something false with confidence, it is called...
questions.note: This is why important answers should be double-checked.

questions.question: The text you type into a chatbot is called a...
questions.note: "Prompt engineering" is the skill of writing these well.

questions.question: Neural networks are loosely inspired by...
questions.note: Layers of simple units, roughly like neurons, pass signals to each other.

questions.question: A large language model like ChatGPT works by predicting...
questions.option_1: the next piece of text (token) in a sequence
questions.note: It has learned which words tend to follow which, at massive scale.

questions.question: Google's AI chatbot is called...
questions.note: It was earlier called Bard.

questions.question: Claude is made by which company?
questions.note: Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI researchers.

questions.question: Microsoft's AI assistant in Windows and Office is called...
questions.note: Clippy was the famous 1990s Office helper; Copilot is its modern successor.

questions.question: Meta's AI model family is called...
questions.note: Meta releases Llama openly, so others can build on it.

questions.question: xAI's chatbot, built into X (Twitter), is called...
questions.note: The name comes from a sci-fi word meaning "to understand deeply".

questions.question: Which of these creates images from a text description?
questions.note: DALL·E is OpenAI's image generator; Midjourney and Stable Diffusion do the same.

questions.question: To get a better answer from a chatbot, you should...
questions.note: Say what you want, who it is for, and the format you prefer.

questions.question: A chatbot gives you a medical or legal answer. What should you do?
questions.option_1: Trust it fully; AI doesn't lie
questions.option_2: Verify it with a qualified professional or trusted source
questions.option_4: Assume AI is wrong about everything
questions.note: Chatbots can sound confident and still be wrong.

questions.question: Which of these should you avoid pasting into a public chatbot?
questions.note: Treat anything you type as potentially stored or seen by the provider.

questions.question: A "deepfake" is...
questions.option_2: a realistic fake audio or video of a real person
questions.note: Deepfakes are used in scams and misinformation.

questions.question: A caller who sounds exactly like your grandson asks you to urgently wire money. The safest first step?
questions.option_1: Send a small amount to test it
questions.option_2: Keep asking the caller personal questions
questions.option_3: Hang up and call your grandson back on his usual number
questions.note: Scammers can clone a voice from seconds of audio. Always call back on a known number.

questions.question: Which task is an AI chatbot genuinely good at?
questions.note: Writing, summarizing, translating and brainstorming are its strengths.

questions.question: CAPTCHA puzzles on websites exist to tell apart...
questions.note: CAPTCHA stands for "Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart".

questions.question: "AGI" stands for...
questions.note: AGI means AI as flexible as a human across most tasks; it does not exist yet.

questions.question: The 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduced which design behind today's chatbots?
questions.note: The "T" in GPT is the Transformer, invented by Google researchers.

questions.question: "Narrow AI" means AI that...
questions.option_2: is good at one specific task
questions.note: Every AI in use today is narrow AI, even the impressive ones.

questions.question: The first global AI Safety Summit in 2023 met at Bletchley Park in which country?
questions.note: Bletchley Park is where Alan Turing's team broke the Enigma code in WWII.

questions.question: Which everyday phone feature typically uses AI?
questions.note: Face unlock matches your face using a learned model.

questions.question: The computer HAL 9000 appears in which film?
questions.note: "I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that." (1968)

questions.question: In the Terminator films, the AI that turns on humanity is called...
questions.note: Ultron is Marvel; Jarvis and Vision are Iron Man's helpers.

questions.question: The humanoid robot "Sophia" was built by which company?
questions.note: Sophia has appeared on talk shows and at the United Nations.

questions.question: DeepMind's AI learned to play Atari games like Breakout mainly by...
questions.option_3: playing thousands of games of trial and error
questions.note: It saw only the screen pixels and the score, like a human would.

questions.question: The word "robot" comes from a 1920 play by which writer?
questions.note: From the Czech word "robota", meaning forced labor.

questions.question: Which sci-fi author created the famous "Three Laws of Robotics"?
questions.note: First law: a robot may not injure a human being.
